newsitem.title: INDIA: Landmine blast kills 3 army personnel in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Landmine blast kills 3 army personnel in Kashmir.

text.p: A landmine blast blamed on separatist militants killed an army major and two soldiers in the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir, police said on Wednesday.
Tuesday's explosion blew up the vehicle in which the three army personnel were travelling, police said.
It occurred on the Srinagar-Jammu highway, near Banihal town, some 190 km (120 miles) east of the state's winter capital of Jammu.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the explosion but police said it was engineered by separatist militants.

In another incident on Tuesday, one paramilitary soldier was killed in a gunfight with members of the militant group Lashkar-E-Toiba in Rajouri district, 170 km (105 miles) west of Jammu, a Border Security Force spokesman said.
Two separatist guerrillas were also killed in the shootout. "Foreign mercenaries" accompanied the militants, police and security officials said.
India has accused Pakistan of aiding Moslem insurgents in the state, but Islamabad says it provides only political and diplomatic support to separatists.
Over a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in the seven-year-old rebellion that broke out in 1990.
